original_question: If N is a closed hyperbolic surface and Omega_i are embedded simply connected billiard tables in N, does there exist a sequence Omega_i for which the length of the shortest closed billiard trajectory Omega_i-sys tends to infinity as i tends to infinity?
target_in_paper: Johanna Bimmermann’s unnumbered question under “Lower bounds via hyperbolic billiards” in her section on the Hofer–Zehnder-capacity problem for disk cotangent bundles over hyperbolic surfaces. It is a subsidiary question suggested as a route toward infiniteness, not the section’s opening capacity question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right ambient setting (a closed hyperbolic surface), the existence of a sequence of billiard tables inside that surface, the use of the billiard-systolic quantity Ω_i-sys, and the asymptotic requirement that this quantity tend to infinity. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: The paper’s standing hypothesis in this section is that the hyperbolic surface N is orientable as well as closed; this should be stated explicitly if the question is to stand alone. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
N should be fixed first, and the sequence should be written explicitly as (Ω_i)_{i≥1} with each Ω_i embedded in that fixed surface N. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Immediately before the question, the paper specifies the relevant class as Ω⊂N open and simply connected; your draft says “embedded simply connected billiard tables,” but for stand-alone fidelity it is better to say “embedded billiard tables Ω_i⊂N, each open and simply connected.” ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The notation Ω_i-sys should be defined in the question itself. The paper introduces it just before the question as the billiard-systolic length attached to Ω_i. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

Your phrase “shortest closed billiard trajectory” is close to the intended meaning, but the paper explicitly warns that for the lower-bound application the notion of billiard trajectory may be slightly relaxed, namely via closed billiard trajectories arising as limits of approximate solutions from the cited approximation schemes. A paper-faithful stand-alone version should not silently impose a stricter interpretation. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The paper does not add extra convexity, Euclidean, or smooth-boundary assumptions at this point, so a refined version should avoid introducing any such extra restrictions. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The question is posed after observing that open simply connected Ω⊂N lift to open subsets of the hyperbolic plane with compact closure; this context explains the geometry being used and can be included parenthetically in a stand-alone rewrite. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
refined_question: Fix an orientable closed hyperbolic surface N. Does there exist a sequence (Ω_i)_{i≥1} of embedded billiard tables Ω_i⊂N, each open and simply connected (hence lifting to an open subset of the hyperbolic plane with compact closure), such that Ω_i-sys→∞ as i→∞, where Ω_i-sys denotes the billiard-systolic length of Ω_i, i.e. the length of the shortest billiard trajectory in the sense used in the paper?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. The exact question appears, unnumbered, under the subheading “Lower bounds via hyperbolic billiards,” after the author introduces Ω-sys for open simply connected Ω⊂N and after the broader opening discussion about Hofer–Zehnder capacity. The faithful refinement therefore just unpacks the fixed ambient surface, the class of domains, and the meaning of Ω_i-sys, while avoiding any extra assumptions not present in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
